summary: Champa Thupten Zongtse worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Affiliated with the University of Göttingen, he is attested there in 1991 and served as a lecturer in 2009.

Chandima Bogahawatta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology, and Shandong University, and held posts at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Chandima Gangodawila, a specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earned a Ph.D. at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura. He held posts at the University of Victoria, Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, and Ateneo de Manila University.

Chandra R. de Silva (1940–2021) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (attested 1991) and as Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at Old Dominion University (attested 2006).

Chandrabhal Tripathi (1929–1996) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen. He held posts at Göttingen, the University of Cologne, and the Free University of Berlin.

Chandrabhan P. Yadav is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. After earning a Ph.D. at Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2021, he served as an assistant professor at Indraprastha College for Women and the National Law School of India University.

Chandradhar Sharma Guleri (1883–1922) worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at the University of Allahabad, he served as head pandit at Mayo College (~1904–1920) and held a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1920–1922).

Chandrika Das is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who pursued a PhD in history at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University Delhi. She held NCWEB guest faculty appointments at the University of Delhi and Miranda House.

Chang Huang is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Wollongong, China University of Geosciences, and the University of Hong Kong. He held postdoctoral positions at the University of Hong Kong and Wageningen University & Research.

Chang-geun Hwang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2000. During his studies, he was advised by Minoru Kiyota, supervised by Morten Schlütter, and taught by Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Changhwan Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Otani University and earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Alexander von Rospatt. He held a professorship at Geumgang University (attested 2013–2017).

Changpei Luo (1899–1958) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He later held academic posts at Xiamen University, Northwest University, Sun Yat-sen University, and Peking University.

Chanju Mun is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Tokyo. His doctoral supervisors included Charles Hallisey, Morten Schlütter, and Masahiro Shimoda.

Channa Li specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, earning a PhD from Leiden University where she studied under Jonathan A. Silk. She has held posts at Leiden University, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Chao-heng Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He has held appointments at Academia Sinica (attested 2018) and the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Charlene Makley is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Norma Diamond and Roy Rappaport. She serves as an associate professor of anthropology at Reed College.

Charles Albert Ferguson (1921–1998) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at the Foreign Service Institute, Harvard, Deccan College, the Center for Applied Linguistics, and Stanford University.

Charles Alexander Moore (1901–1967) was a philosopher who studied at Yale and Visva-Bharati universities. He taught at Yale and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and founded and edited the journal Philosophy East and West.
Charles Alfred Bell (1870–1945) was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He was educated at Winchester College and New College, Oxford, and was a Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society.

Charles Arthur Roe (1841–1927) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at Merton College, served in the Indian Civil Service (~1863–1898), and was Vice-Chancellor of Panjab University in 1895.
